security_concerns.title: Malformed historical context JSON blocks all upload admission
security_concerns.details: fast_quota_snapshot executes json_extract(context_json, '$.analysisTier') without guarding malformed JSON. The snapshot is invoked for every new job, including normal-tier submissions, so one malformed jobs.context_json row for that account causes SQLite OperationalError ('malformed JSON') and prevents all further uploads rather than treating the row as uncountable/legacy. Reproduced against an isolated temporary SQLite DB with a synthetic failed job containing context_json='{bad json'; fast_quota_snapshot raised sqlite3.OperationalError.
security_concerns.impact: Account-level denial of service for uploads when legacy/corrupt/imported job context is malformed. No production data was accessed.
security_concerns.reproduction: Create synthetic account x and job j in a temporary database, insert context_json='{bad json', then call queue.fast_quota_snapshot({'id':'x','role':'user'}).

logic_errors.title: Delivered native client does not honor Retry-After
logic_errors.details: Inspected delivered android-client UploadWorker.java and JagaSyncPlugin.java; neither contains Retry-After handling. The frontend offline-sync.js reads Retry-After and applies a retry delay, but the handoff's broader assertion that native sync already honors the header is not supported by the delivered 2.1.2 native source. Backend emits a valid delta-seconds header; native retries therefore use their existing behavior rather than this server-provided reset time.
logic_errors.impact: Native/offline submissions may retry before the quota resets or wait using a generic policy. This does not bypass the server quota.
logic_errors.reproduction: Search the two delivered Java sources for 'Retry-After'; no matches. Compare frontend/offline-sync.js lines 45-47, which parses it.

suggestions: Guard JSON extraction using json_valid(context_json), e.g. CASE WHEN json_valid(context_json) THEN json_extract(...) END; add malformed/null/valid-context coverage for both fast and normal admission.

Either implement Retry-After handling in the native client before a future native release or narrow the handoff claim to the web/offline-sync client; verify against the actual release artifact when available.
The frontend retry delay clamps server Retry-After to one hour; that is an intentional/operational behavior to verify if long waits are expected, since a next-midnight value can exceed that limit.

executed_checks.command: unified diff of six reviewed backend files against JagaKebond-2.1.2/app/backend/ in delivered source ZIP
executed_checks.result: Diffs reviewed for the quota changes: authoritative role/active admission in transaction; cap calculation and Jakarta window; normal-mode exclusion; legacy daily_quota compatibility handling; and 429 Retry-After.

scope_notes: Read-only review. No edits to source/tests, production imports/data/environment, credentials, or network services. Only this review report is created. Quota deletion/purge was traced: purge deletes only acked terminal rows after long retention, so it cannot remove current-day admissions. The per-admission role read and SQLite writer transaction serialize quota counting/insertion; idempotent replay is checked before cap rejection. Jakarta midnight window uses timezone-aware local date boundaries. Registration forces user; priority role is accepted only through admin account management and receives no require_admin privilege. Legacy stored daily_quota does not control caps.
